papers.title: PrEP Use and Willingness Cascades Among Transgender Women in 11 Asian Countries: Findings From the PrEP APPEAL Cross-Sectional Online Survey.
papers.journal: Journal of the International AIDS Society
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transgender women in Asia face a high HIV burden, yet remain underrepresented in pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) research. Despite increases in PrEP availability, uptake among trans women remains low. This study examines PrEP awareness, use, and willingness among trans women across 11 Asian countries. METHODS: Data were drawn from the 2022 PrEP Product Awareness, Preferences, and Past Experiences Among Transgender Women and Men Who Have Sex with Men (PrEP APPEAL) study, a multi-country cross-sectional online survey. Two PrEP cascades were constructed: one assessing use (awareness, lifetime use, current use) and the other assessing willingness (risk, interest, and willingness to pay). Logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with lifetime PrEP use and willingness to use PrEP. RESULTS: Of 1178 trans women participants, 80.0% (n = 942) had heard of PrEP. Among those who were PrEP-aware, 62.6% (n = 590/942) reported ever using it, and of these, 78.1% (n = 461/590) were current users. Among PrEP-naïve participants classified as at risk of HIV (n = 265), 60.0% (n = 159/265) were willing to initiate PrEP, yet only 34.0% (n = 54/159) were also willing to pay. Lifetime PrEP use was positively associated with wider country-level PrEP access (aOR = 4.34; 95% CI: 3.03-6.21), genital surgery (aOR = 1.54; 1.03-2.31), current romantic relationship (aOR = 1.65; 1.19-2.29), as well as reporting sex work (aOR = 1.51; 1.05-2.18), condomless sex (aOR = 1.76; 1.28-2.42), chemsex (aOR = 1.98; 1.36-2.87), and a recent sexually transmitted infection diagnosis (aOR = 2.28; 1.45-3.59) within the past 6 months. papers.title: Effects of electroacupuncture on the LOC103691336-miR-138-5p axis and anti-Müllerian hormone levels in a rat model of polycystic ovarian syndrome.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Electroacupuncture has been shown to effectively reduce anti-Müllerian hormone levels and improve follicular development in polycystic ovary syndrome. However, the mechanism of action is yet to be deciphered. Long noncoding RNAs have been shown to play an important role in polycystic ovary syndrome and function as competing endogenous RNAs to regulate target genes. Therefore, the aim of this study was to observe whether the effect of electroacupuncture on anti-Müllerian hormone involves modulation of the long noncoding RNA LOC103691336. METHODS: A polycystic ovary syndrome rat model was established and treated with low-frequency electroacupuncture at CV3 and CV4. Estrous cycle, ovarian morphology, and the levels of anti-Müllerian hormone and testosterone in the serum and ovaries were measured. Follicular granulosa cells of rats in each group were collected for in vitro experiments. High-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics methods were applied to analyze anti-Müllerian hormone-related long noncoding RNAs, and LOC103691336 was identified as the long noncoding RNA most closely related to anti-Müllerian hormone. Silencing of LOC103691336 was applied to observe its effect on the expression of anti-Müllerian hormone. Argonaute 2 RNA immunoprecipitation assays and RNA pulldown were used to observe whether LOC103691336 functions as a miR-138-5p sponge to regulate anti-Müllerian hormone. RESULTS: Estrus cycle and ovarian morphology were improved by electroacupuncture. Expression levels of anti-Müllerian hormone and testosterone were significantly reduced in ovarian tissues and peripheral serum (P < 0.01 and P < 0.05). High-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis showed a close relationship between LOC103691336 and anti-Müllerian hormone. papers.title: How Sexually Objectifying Others Undermines Connection and Collaboration.
papers.journal: Perspectives on psychological science : a journal of the Association for Psychological Science
papers.abstract: Sexual objectification is widely recognized as a driver of gender inequality, harming women by reducing them to bodies and undermining their agency. Yet psychological science has rarely asked a consequential question: Does sexual objectification also harm the individuals who objectify? In this theoretical article, we reframe objectification as not only oppressive but also self-undermining. Drawing from social, cognitive, organizational, and relationship science, we argue that objectifying others can compromise the capacity to form close relationships, collaborate effectively, and function well in social and professional life. These costs are traced to four mechanisms-cognitive load, face-body attentional trade-off, goal-based perception, and dehumanization. These mechanisms are proposed to operate as parallel, mutually reinforcing pathways that converge on social miscalibration. The framework further motivates a methodological agenda for studying objectification as a dynamic, dyadic process embedded in ongoing interaction. By foregrounding the objectifiers' costs, we extend existing theories and highlight objectification as a mode of social perception that degrades the very relationships and institutions on which objectifiers rely. Identifying these costs offers an additional reason to reduce objectification, one that complements rather than replaces concern for the harms it inflicts on targets.

papers.title: Dopamine release-associated striatal blood oxygenation and whole-brain dynamics during associative learning.
papers.abstract: Dopaminergic signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) is central to reward-based learning, but its relationship to brain-wide hemodynamics remains unclear. Using concurrent fMRI and dopamine photometry in awake, behaving mice, we reveal that associative learning induces a gradual temporal shift in NAc blood oxygenation responses that mirrors dopamine release dynamics. This shift emerges with cue-reward learning and extends across a distributed network encompassing the lateral septal complex, as well as prefrontal, insular, and hypothalamic regions. Further, dopamine transients tightly correspond with local blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) signals, and variations in reward value modulate delayed BOLD responses in both the NAc and additional subcortical structures. Regressing out the measured dopaminergic signal abolishes this reward-related modulation, suggesting that BOLD signals track dopaminergic reward prediction. These findings reveal a close relationship between dopamine signaling and widespread changes in brain activity during learning.

papers.title: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) Victimization and Post-Breakup Stalking Victimization Among Korean Women: A Latent Class Analysis.
papers.abstract: Stalking is a highly debated social issue in Korea. Using data from the Violence Against Women: Focused on Intimate Partner Violence study, this research identifies patterns of IPV victimization and examines how these patterns are associated with post-breakup stalking among Korean women formerly in romantic relationships. It also explores various factors that may influence different IPV victimization patterns. Based on the findings, the study offers policy recommendations, including the development of educational programs and risk assessment tools to prevent future IPV and stalking victimization among Korean women.

papers.title: Finding Love in the Black Box: Algorithm Awareness on Dating Apps.
papers.abstract: Most dating apps use algorithms to match users to one another, but are not fully transparent about how their recommender systems work. In turn, users have varying degrees of awareness of matching algorithms. Unfortunately, little is known about how awareness of algorithmic functioning relates to online dating. This research examined the relationship between algorithm awareness, trust in algorithms, and satisfaction with the quality of matches. A survey was conducted among 500 users of the Dutch dating app Breeze, presented to respondents within the app itself. Relationships were estimated with structural equation modeling. Higher algorithm awareness was associated with more trust in algorithms, which positively related to satisfaction with the quality of matches. This mediated association between awareness and satisfaction with matches suggested that awareness of matching algorithms is associated with better outcomes of dating app use. This research contributes to the limited literature on human-algorithm interaction on dating apps. Overall, the results suggest that algorithm awareness may be a relevant part of the online dating experience.

papers.title: Doing "a lot of learning myself": how college students learn about sexual and dating relationships.
papers.journal: Journal of American college health : J of ACH
papers.abstract: Objective: The purpose of this study was to explore how first-year college students learn about dating and sexual relationships prior to and during their first semester of college. Participants: Twenty-seven first-year students from two large public research universities participated in this study. Methods: Participants engaged in an initial interview at the beginning of their first-semester of college, completed eight weekly journal prompts throughout the semester, and participated in a follow-up focus group or interview at the end of the semester. Results: Students learn about sex and dating by 1) directly receiving information, 2) observing others and the media, 3) engaging in sexual and dating relationships themselves, and 4) filling gaps through searching for information. Conclusions: Employing the concept of conscientization and social cognitive theory, we demonstrate that students learn more from experiences and their family and peers' behaviors, as school-based education does not critically engage students to deepen their understanding. We discuss implications for campus sex education and sexual violence prevention programming.

papers.title: Association of statin use with severe urogenital symptoms and lower sexual function in postmenopausal women: a cross-sectional study.
papers.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between statin use, urogenital symptoms and sexual function in postmenopausal women. METHOD: This cross-sectional study included 1184 postmenopausal women from nine Latin American countries. Participants were classified according to statin use. Urogenital symptoms were assessed using the urogenital domain of the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) and sexual function was evaluated with the Female Sexual Function Index-6 (FSFI-6). Multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with severe urogenital symptoms and lower sexual function. RESULTS: Of the participants, 307 (25.9%) were statin users. According to the MRS, statin users reported significantly higher frequencies of vaginal dryness, urinary complaints and sexual problems as well as a greater prevalence of severe urogenital symptoms than non-users (24.4% vs. 12.3%; p < 0.001). They also showed poorer performance across all FSFI-6 domains and a higher prevalence of lower sexual function (78.5% vs. 64.4%; p < 0.001). After adjustment for confounders, statin use remained independently associated with severe urogenital symptoms (odds ratio [OR] 1.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-2.50) and lower sexual function (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.07-1.99). CONCLUSIONS: Statin use was independently associated with severe urogenital symptoms and lower sexual function in postmenopausal women. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causality. Sexual and urinary symptoms are common during postmenopause and may negatively affect quality of life, intimate relationships and emotional well-being. papers.title: A stir-bar adsorbent of polydopamine-coated melamine sponge incorporating MIL-125 for the extraction of estrogens in milk.
papers.abstract: Estrogens are used to increase milk production but can accumulate in the human body, eventually causing adverse effects. To extract estrogens from milk, a melamine sponge stir bar adsorbent was fabricated in a dual-polymer functionalization process, using polydopamine (PDA), and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) combined with MIL-125 (MS-PDA@PVA-MIL-125). PDA introduced additional hydroxyl and amino groups to the adsorbent surface, increasing the number of active sites available to the target analytes. PVA acted as a binder to anchor MIL-125 into the composite structure. MIL-125 was employed as the active adsorption material, significantly enhancing the extraction efficiency of estrogens through hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interaction, and π-π interaction. The composite adsorbent extracted estradiol, ethinyl estradiol, estrone, and hexestrol from milk samples in a stir bar sorptive extraction (SBSE) procedure. The extracted estrogens were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with diode-array detector. The developed method demonstrated good linearity from 1.50 to 100 μg L⁻¹ with a limit of detection of 0.50 μg L⁻¹. Recoveries from spiked milk samples were in the range of 80 to 104%, with RSDs less than 6%. This innovative design provides high extraction efficiency, simple preparation, self-stirring capability, cost-effectiveness, and good environmental friendliness.

papers.title: Barriers to entry: A participatory science study of tick identification, monitoring, and physical barriers to reduce tick bites on horses.
papers.abstract: Equine tick-borne diseases pose increasing challenges due to climate change and expanding tick geographical ranges. With no vaccines available for Lyme disease or equine anaplasmosis in horses, tick bite prevention remains the primary control method. This two-year study evaluated tick species composition on horses in Pennsylvania and assessed the effectiveness of physical barriers for tick prevention through community-based participatory research. The study engaged horse owners as research partners. Year 1 (2022) established baseline tick surveillance across 45 participants with 60 horses, conducting weekly tick checks from April to June. Year 2 (2023) evaluated physical barrier interventions using 50 horses assigned to three treatments: No Treatment (control), Physical Barrier (Untreated), and Physical Barrier (Treated with permethrin), with twice-weekly surveillance. A total of 413 ticks were collected, with species composition shifts between years. Species recovered included American dog ticks (Dermacentor variabilis), blacklegged ticks (Ixodes scapularis), and longhorned ticks (Haemaphysalis longicornis), which were detected for the first time in one of the counties in the study region. Tick attachment occurred across eight body locations and differed significantly between years. Physical barriers, particularly untreated fly boots and masks, were associated with reduced tick attachment. Comprehensive whole-body surveillance remains essential given consistent tick distribution across anatomical regions.

papers.title: Site-Selective Anion-Cation Regulation of Sulfide Electrolyte Enables Low-Pressure Dendrite-Suppressed All-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries.
papers.abstract: Achieving stable sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium batteries with Li metal anodes and high-capacity cathodes under low stack pressure is highly desirable for high-energy-density energy storage, but remains challenging because of unstable solid-solid interfaces and dendrite-induced short circuits. Here, we develop a site-selective anion-cation regulation strategy for argyrodite Li6PS5Cl electrolyte to couple framework stabilization with interphase chemistry, enabling long-term dendrite-suppressed cycling under low stack pressure. Al3+ substitution for P5+ forms AlS4 -related local units and strengthens local Al-S bonding, stabilizing the sulfide framework against redox decomposition. Cl- incorporation into the 4a/4d anion sublattice promotes Li+ transport, delivering a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 7.22 mS cm-1. More importantly, F/Cl regulation redirects the interfacial decomposition pathway from a Li2S-rich/LiCl interphase toward a LiF/LiCl-rich and Li2S-poor passivation layer, with exposed LiF/LiCl (200) planes that exhibit stronger interfacial adhesion with Li metal. Benefiting from this coupled framework-interphase regulation, Li | LAPSCF-Cl | Li symmetric cells cycle for over 8000 h at 0.5 mA cm-2 at 3 MPa and support stable cycling of both NCM811 and sulfur cathodes paired with Li metal under a relatively low pressure of 30 MPa.

papers.title: Operationalizing deployment history: Three approaches to examining associations with military couples' marital satisfaction.
papers.journal: Military psychology : the official journal of the Division of Military Psychology, American Psychological Association
papers.abstract: Military life, especially deployment, introduces stressors that extend beyond the individual service member, often influencing partners and family members. The spillover-crossover model suggests that work-related stressors can spill over to affect individual well-being and cross over to intimate partners, shaping couple dynamics. However, findings on the relationship between deployment and relationship satisfaction are mixed, perhaps in part because of different ways of measuring deployment history. Using dyadic survey data from 285 U.S.-based military couples with an active-duty service member and their civilian spouse, three separate path models were tested to assess the association between deployment and marital satisfaction with three different operationalizations of deployment history. Associations with other military characteristics, including the number of permanent change of station moves, years of service, and branch were also investigated in these models. Service members who reported at least one combat deployment reported higher marital satisfaction than those who had experienced only non-combat deployments. However, when service members were injured during a combat deployment mission, their spouses reported lower marital satisfaction. Surprisingly, of the other military characteristics examined, more PCS moves were consistently related to greater marital satisfaction. Overall, the results indicated that these military families were largely resilient and successful at navigating the relationship challenges of military life, suggesting a strength-based approach for efforts with military couples. Practical implications are also considered, particularly for families with an injured service member. Limitations and future directions for research are also shared.

papers.title: Breathing Easy Together: How Positive Airway Pressure Adherence Benefits Both Patients and Partners.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Emerging research highlights the interdependence of sleep within couples and the impact of sleep disorders on couples' relationship quality; however, most sleep treatments are focused solely on the individual. WePAP is a dyadic, behavioral treatment to promote positive airway pressure (PAP) adherence in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and sleep quality in both patients and partners. This analysis examines the impact of WePAP compared to Information Control (IC) on the couples' relationship quality. Across treatment conditions, we examined whether greater PAP adherence associates with better sleep and relationship quality, higher quality of life (QOL) and lower depression in both patients and partners. METHODS: Patients who were diagnosed with OSA and prescribed PAP and their partners were randomly assigned to WePAP or information control (IC). Relationship quality (satisfaction and conflict), QOL, and depression were assessed in both partners via validated questionnaires at baseline and at 3-months. Sleep duration and efficiency were assessed via one-week of actigraphy in both partners. Primary analyses evaluated changes over time and between-group differences in relationship quality, from baseline to 3-month follow-up. Secondary analyses employed mixed models to assess whether greater patient PAP adherence predicts better relationship quality, mental health, and QoL, and greater sleep duration and efficiency. RESULTS: The analytic sample included 32 midlife and older adult couples (age m=62.97; SD=9.04). There were no significant within-group or between-group changes in relationship satisfaction or conflict in patients or partners. Greater PAP adherence was associated with higher levels of relationship satisfaction and QOL and lower levels of relationship conflict and depressive symptoms, and shorter sleep duration for patients and partners. papers.title: Magnitude, trajectory and determinants of antenatal depressive symptoms in Adama Town and East Shewa Zone, Ethiopia: evidence from a prospective longitudinal eCohort survey.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Antenatal depression is a significant yet under-recognised global public health concern that affects a substantial proportion of women in Ethiopia. This study aimed to examine the magnitude, trajectory and determinants of depressive symptoms among pregnant women. DESIGN: A prospective longitudinal study design was conducted between April 2023 and February 2024. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: The study was conducted in Adama Town and the East Shewa Zone of the Oromia Region, Ethiopia. A total of 933 pregnant women who visited the health facility for their first ANC visit were recruited and followed throughout their pregnancy. PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: Antenatal depressive symptoms were measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 through face-to-face interviews and monthly phone calls. The trajectory and determinants of antenatal depressive symptoms were assessed using group-based trajectory modelling and generalised estimating equations. RESULTS: The study found that overall, 30.5% of participants experienced antenatal depressive symptoms, with a lower prevalence at the first measurement point (24.2%) and higher prevalence at the second measurement point (36.9%). Antenatal depressive symptoms were higher during the first trimester (35.6%) compared with the second (19.8%) and third (13.2%) at baseline, and the pattern was consistent across the monthly follow-up period. Moreover, 11.6% of pregnant women had a trajectory of mild-to-moderate depressive symptoms over time. papers.title: Creating nurturing environments: Addressing domestic violence to improve early childhood development outcomes.
papers.abstract: Optimal early childhood development (ECD) is critical for long-term health and economic well-being. Over a quarter of young children across low- and middle-income countries face developmental delays. Domestic violence (DV) is harmful to children's healthy development. Using a difference-in-differences design across 38,955 African children aged 36-59 months, this study examines the impact of laws prohibiting DV on ECD status. We find that DV laws significantly increase the probability of being developmentally on track for children born after enactment by 27.7 percentage points. Children with partial exposure also showed a 24.1 percentage point increase. These gains are primarily driven by advancements in the socio-emotional domain.

papers.title: Heat, home-based assault and domestic and family violence injuries: Evidence from hospital emergency department presentations.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated temperatures have been associated with increased interpersonal violence, yet evidence from hospital, health-sector data remains limited. Guided by theories linking environmental conditions, social interactions and violence-related harm, this study examines home-based assault injuries, including domestic and family violence (DFV) related injuries, presenting to emergency departments (ED) in Victoria, the only state in Australia with mandatory recording of rich data on injuries enabling assessment of the relationship with heat exposure. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of the Victorian Emergency Minimum Dataset identified home-based assault injury presentations (2009-2024) and DFV-related injury presentations (2016-2024). Daily temperature and heat-stress metrics were derived from Australian Gridded Climate Data and time and place aligned with ED presentations. Associations between heat exposure and injury presentations were examined using generalized linear mixed models. RESULTS: A total of 28,637 home-based assault injuries and 10,194 DFV-related injuries were identified. Home-based assault injuries occurred more frequently during summer, weekends and holiday periods. After adjustment for temporal and contextual factors, unusually hot days were associated with a 5.7% increase in home-based assault injury presentations, while days exceeding 30°C were associated with a 6.7% increase. DFV-related injuries demonstrated similar temporal patterns, although associations with heat exposure were not statistically significant after adjustment for season. CONCLUSIONS: Higher temperatures were associated with increased presentations for home-based assault injuries.
